account.name: Northpine
account.industry: transportation, logistics, supply chain and storage

dossier.summary: Northpine audits freight invoices for mid-market shippers and recovers overcharges from carriers. It charges a share of what it recovers. The site names Harlow Foods and Copperleaf Home as customers.
dossier.why_now: Added parcel invoice audits for FedEx and UPS in September.

strategy.intro: Northpine gets paid out of money shippers already lost, so the pitch can be close to risk-free. The campaign goes after the people who sign off on freight invoices and asks one question: how much of last quarter's freight spend did anyone check line by line?
strategy.audience: Logistics and finance managers at manufacturers and distributors shipping more than 2 million dollars of freight a year. We skip retailers with in-house audit teams; they already do this.
strategy.offer: A free overcharge scan on 90 days of invoices. Northpine only gets paid on what it recovers, so the scan has no downside for them.
strategy.channels: Email leads, since freight managers live in their inbox. LinkedIn is the second touch for the finance side, who are easier to reach there.
strategy.goal: Ten scans started in the first two weeks. Each scan that finds money turns into a contract almost on its own.

data.segment_notes: Logistics managers go first because they see the invoices every week and can say yes to a scan without a meeting.
data.sampling_criteria: Logistics and transportation managers at US manufacturers and distributors with 100 to 1,000 people.

body: Harrow Valve ships heavy parts by LTL across 30 states, which is where accessorial charges slip through.

Want a free scan of your last 90 days of invoices?
